_: AD-22. The Impact page's own editorial content. THE FIGURES ARE NOT HERE ON PURPOSE — every number on the page is read out of data/work/**, so /impact cannot disagree with the item page it came from. That was the defect class that had the situation index showing 412 while the Air page said 387. Anything in this file that names a figure names it by (kind, slug, label) and the build resolves it; a reference that does not resolve is a build failure, not a blank.

frame._: Chosen on measurement. 2400x1600 and TRULY landscape (EXIF orientation 1), with the highest RMS contrast of any frame in the library at 92 — and contrast, not brightness, is what lets a subject read through the halftone screen. The crop is 80%, chosen by rendering six candidate strips and looking at them rather than by the contrast metric alone: the metric preferred 19%, which fills the band with the placard's own lettering and puts CLEAN AIR IS OUR RIGHT in direct typographic competition with the headline. At 80% the placard is reduced to a bright edge and the band is a row of faces — people, countable, which is what this page is about. The two frames tried before it, trekkers-hillside and snow-trek-group, both carry EXIF orientation 6: they are 1500x2000 PORTRAIT as a browser lays them out, and putting a portrait photograph in a 1440x360 letterbox showed a thin horizontal sliver of a tall image. That, and not tonality, is what "the image is not visible" was. The subject also earns its place: students with hand-lettered placards is people, countable, and the nearest thing in our archive to the policy claim this page is still waiting on.

masthead.lead: Every figure Swechha can source, on one page, with the span it counts and where it comes from. What is not here is the one number an impact page normally exists to print, and the reason is the whole of this page.

refuse.head:
Why there is
no total
refuse.lead: The figures below count overlapping groups of people over periods that do not line up. Added together they would be a larger number and a false one, so they are not added together.
refuse.overlap_intro: Four of them, to show the shape of the problem. One young person can be inside all four at once:

overlap.label: Youth leaders who have walked it
Girls and boys through the programme

argument.h: The populations overlap, and nothing records by how much
argument.p: A volunteer who walked an eco-walk is in the first two rows. A girl who came through ME to WE and then led a Yatra is in the last two. Nobody has ever recorded which person is in which programme, so the size of the overlap is not merely unpublished — it was never collected.

argument.h: The periods do not share a denominator
argument.p: One of those four is annual, one is two decades, one is since 2004 and one is thirteen years. A sum over four different spans is not a quantity. It is four quantities printed next to each other with a plus sign between them.

argument.h: So the register is held open instead
argument.p: Every figure keeps the span it counts and the source it came from, and it is read against its neighbours rather than into them. That is more work for the reader than one number would be. It is also the only version of this page that is true.

refuse.rule: This is not modesty and it is not a hedge. The same refusal governs the readings: the situation index will not average six units either, and says so on its face. An organisation that declines to average micrograms and milligrams does not get to add up children.

pair.head:
Two numbers,
one programme
pair.lead: Bridge the Gap publishes two figures that a reader will assume are rival versions of the same count. They are not. They are answers to two different questions, and the gap between them is the most useful thing on this page.

rows.h: One counts reach. The other counts effect.
rows.p: The larger figure counts children in a school the programme entered. The smaller counts children who sat the sessions. Reach is what an organisation can claim; effect is what it can be held to. Both belong on the page, labelled, because publishing only the first is advertising and publishing only the second hides the scale of the work.

rows.h: One is counted. The other is derived.
rows.p: The smaller figure comes out of the organisation's own record of schools and students. The larger is arithmetic — schools a year, times years, times the children in a school — and the middle term of that is written down nowhere we can cite. So it carries a dotted rule and the word Modelled, and the counted figures carry a solid one.

rows.h: Which is why a withdrawn figure is not the same as a derived one
rows.p: This page once carried twenty-five thousand children, eighty-five schools and twelve hundred mentors, captioned as verified. None of the three could be traced to any record held anywhere, and all three are withdrawn. The difference is not the size of the number. It is that a derivation shows its arithmetic and an unsourced claim has none to show.

register.head:
Every figure
we can source
register.lead: All of them, by kind. Under each label the rule is solid where the figure was counted and dotted where it was modelled. Each one carries the span it counts and the source it came from — and nothing appears here that is not already on the page it belongs to.
register.note: Eleven of the section's twenty-three entries carry no figure at all and are not padded with one. Seven campaigns, three events and one project are names and holes until somebody produces a number for them.

waiting.head:
Four claims
waiting on
one number each
waiting.lead: These were given by the Executive Director on 22 August 2026 and every one of them is almost certainly true. None can be published as a figure yet, for the same reason in each case: a claim without a quantity and a span is a sentence, not a reading. They are named here rather than left out.

claims.what: Air detox gardens. The term is now settled — it is the Executive Director's own — but the count is not. The project page currently ships the source documents' word, Airshed Park, and carries no figure for them at all; its only airshed number is the single Vasant Kunj park.
claims.unlocks: How many air detox gardens there are. One number promotes this from a sentence to a figure and settles a terminology question open since 21 August.

claims.what: More than a hundred acres restored, through permaculture and plantation. There is no acreage anywhere in the register except the farm's own — and that one is already contradictory: the Farm School page says five acres, the front page of this site says forty.
claims.unlocks: The span this covers, and a ruling on forty against five. Three different acreages on one site cannot all be read, and this is the one that makes the other two urgent.

claims.what: Garbage taken out of the Yamuna. The claim is confirmed; the quantity is not. The reading that runs on the front page of this site — six thousand eight hundred and ninety tonnes out of the river — appears in no source document we hold, and the cell carrying it has never linked anywhere.
claims.unlocks: Whether that tonnage is the number, and since when. If it is, the oldest broken link on this site gets its destination and this page gets its strongest single figure.

claims.what: Policies influenced. This would be the first entry in the whole register that records an outcome rather than a count of people, sites or material — and on this site's own terms it is worth more than any of them, because it is an effect and the rest is reach.
claims.unlocks: One policy, named: the instrument, the year, and what Swechha did. One named policy is worth more here than five unnamed ones, and it is the only thing that would change what this page leads with.

sheet.head: What it looked like
sheet.lead: Frames from our own archive, across the four kinds. Each says what it shows and nothing more.
sheet.note: None of these is captioned to a figure above it. Which programme a photograph belongs to is not recorded in our archive, and a frame presented as evidence for a number it was never linked to would be the same defect this page is about.

sheet._: CELL ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING. Cells 1 and 8 span two columns at 8:3, so both must hold a genuinely wide frame — the first build put clean-air-protest (1.50) and community-meal (0.75, portrait) in them and cropped both to slivers. Positions 1 and 8 are now 2.17 and 2.45. Every other cell is 4:3, where a portrait frame crops honestly. Gated in the generator against the library, which is itself now checked against the files.

act.head: Hold us to it
act.lead: A register is only worth the checking. Three ways in, and the middle one is the one that changes what is on this page.

doors.p: Fifteen pages, four kinds. Every figure above, on the page it belongs to, with what it does not say.
Four claims above are one figure short. If you hold a register, a roll or a receipt that settles one, it goes on the page with your name on the source line.
Six situations in the world outside, each against the limit somebody published for it.
